about: Dissolved acetylene (C₂H₂) is acetylene gas dissolved in acetone inside a porous mass in the cylinder, which makes it safe to store and transport. Burned with oxygen it gives the hottest common fuel-gas flame, so it is used for oxy-acetylene welding, cutting, brazing and heating.

Acetylene becomes unstable at higher pressures: draw it at no more than about 1 bar (15 psi) line pressure, keep cylinders upright and fit flashback arrestors. Never use copper or high-copper alloy fittings with acetylene.

faq.question: What is dissolved acetylene used for?
faq.answer: Dissolved acetylene is burned with oxygen for welding, flame cutting, brazing and heating of metals in workshops, fabrication yards and construction sites.
